name: IN-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Yakym with large fundraising advantage ($5.2M raised)
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~96%
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The district's R+13 lean, Yakym's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and markets pricing a Republican win near 96% all point the same way, with no polling or ratings suggesting movement toward Decio. A modest Democratic shift from the baseline reflects her nontrivial fundraising, but the race remains firmly Republican-favored.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending in the district would be the first signal the race is competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North-central Indiana's second district is solidly Republican ground, and incumbent Rudy Yakym is seeking another term after first winning the seat in a 2022 special election. He has raised over $5 million and holds a large cash advantage over Democrat Jamee Decio, who has raised about $356,000. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's strong Republican lean, Yakym's incumbency and financial edge, and prediction markets that price his win around 96%. Decio's fundraising gives her a credible but uphill path in a district that has consistently favored Republicans.
